title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) measuring the marginal detection benefit of automated sandboxed emulation over a strong deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Using the declared model (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, run accounting diagnostics, an explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and concise reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for intent-driven NetOps tasks (intent→configuration, workflow synthesis) and as AIOps co-pilots. Operational trustworthiness for such agentic pipelines depends heavily on surrounding deterministic validators, verifiers, and sandboxed execution to detect and mitigate incorrect or unsafe outputs [1], [2]. Prior work documents generate→validate→repair architectures and prototype runtime emulation but provides limited quantitative cross-vendor estimates of the marginal value added by sandboxed emulation over strong static validators. We therefore posed the preregistered confirmatory research question: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest was 0.20 (20 percentage points) for the aggregated paired difference.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system reports situate LLMs within NetOps/AIOps workflows and emphasize workflow-centred mitigations—static validators, verifiers, and sandboxed execution—to reduce operational risk [1], [2]. Tool papers and verification transfers show that emulation or formal analysis can expose runtime failures missed by static checks in some domains [2], [3]. Empirical studies in code and configuration generation demonstrate that external verifiers often improve correctness but that LLMs alone poorly locate their own reasoning errors [3]. These findings motivate paired, workflow-level measurements: rather than ranking LLMs, our study quantifies the marginal guarded-stage detection effect in a narrowly scoped, preregistered regime and places that measurement in the context of validator coverage and task construction.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and primary estimand. We froze a machine-readable preregistration before execution (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). Design: paired-binary (shared_initial_candidate semantics). For each pair a single sampled initial candidate was produced and reused by both baseline and guarded analyses; therefore any between-condition discordance can only originate from (i) guarded-stage emulation observations revealing violations not covered by the static validator, or (ii) the permitted downstream repair-stage invocation recorded in the run accounting. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistered minimum effect-of-interest used in power planning was 0.20 (20 percentage points) targeting ≈80% power under conservative baseline-rate assumptions.
sections.results:
Execution and sample accounting. Confirmatory execution completed without technical exclusions: planned episodes = 1440; completed episodes = 1440; complete paired records = 720 (one shared initial generation and separate baseline/guarded analyses per pair). Model call accounting (execution manifest) records model_calls_used = 721: stage_counts show shared_initial_generation = 720 and repair = 1. No failed episodes or irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred in the confirmatory set; missingness_summary reports zero missing or excluded pairs.

Primary outcome and exact statistics. The archived paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) records n11 = 719, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI with 10000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numerical outputs and CSV artifacts are archived in the execution bundle (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv).

Discordant-pair attribution and run-audit pointer. The single discordant item (n10 = 1) is traceable in the archived execution artifacts. Independent verifiers should locate the unique record in execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 = df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8) that has baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; that entry contains the pair_id and the per-episode validator and emulation traces. Analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (artifact path and hash archived) corroborates provider_call_audit showing exactly one repair-stage invocation and the stage accounting (shared_initial_generation = 720; repair = 1). We intentionally do not reproduce pair_id textually here to avoid duplicating long per-episode traces; the precise mapping is available via the canonical execution/raw_results.jsonl artifact referenced above.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Archived representative task entries (artifact_examples: task-000001 through task-000006) illustrate typical candidate normalization, validator before/after states, parsed command counts, and validator vi olation counts. In these representative excerpts the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) reports violation_count = 0 and score = 1 for most candidates; this pattern generalizes across the confirmatory set and explains the observed baseline ceiling. Validator traces also include per-episode difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) enabling stratified exploratory analyses recorded in archived artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregated benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded explanatory factors. First, a validator ceiling effect: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 covered the syntactic and explicit semantic misconfigurations encoded in the synthetic task bank, yielding baseline success rate ≈0.9986. Second, task curation: confirmatory items were parser-validated synthetic tasks designed to exercise workflow policies but not adversarially constructed to evade the validator; this concentrates items inside the validator's coverage envelope. Third, design semantics and accounting: shared_initial_candidate semantics force identical initial candidates across conditions so guarded-only detection can occur only through emulation-observed behaviors or a repair-stage run; provider_call_audit shows exactly one repair-stage call consistent with the single n10 discordance.

Operational interpretation and boundary conditions. Our finding implies that when a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs conform to the validator's expected patterns, guarded sandboxed emulation may add negligible aggregate detection value. This conditional conclusion should not be generalized beyond the tested regime. In operational scenarios with noisy natural-language intents, adversarial alterations, complex stateful protocol interactions, or validator gaps (different vendor behaviors), guarded runtime checks and high‑fidelity emulation can produce substantive added value. The archived per-episode traces suggest follow-up experiments: (a) adversarially perturbed task banks, (b) multi-validator ensembles, and (c) higher-fidelity emulators to expand the coverage envelope where emulation could meaningfully increase detection.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; shared_initial_candidate semantics mean archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping via execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 = df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8). We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and synthetic task curation and recommend targeted regimes—adversarial tasks, multi-vendor task banks, and multiple validator families—where guarded stages may provide substantive added value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validators.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrow near-zero finding for this experimental regime.
Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; provider_call_audit and reconciliation artifacts document these checks.
